item.title: LOT-114: deterministic FilteredPosts app tests (#467)
item.body:
## Issue
Closes #467
Claim: cloud/fix-filter-tests
LOT-114

## What and why
The FilteredPosts tests hit the 60 s suite limit at random on a loaded parallel simulator clone. Causes removed (tests only, `FilteredPostsModel` untouched, no race found there):
- `settle()` polled `isRunning || isAdvancing` with `Task.yield()` on the main actor → now `await model.lastRun?.value`, resumed by the run's own completion.
- `ReaderGate.untilArrived()` polled with `Task.yield()` → now a continuation resumed by `wait()` (shared helper; other users call it once per gate and keep working).
- `aRunCancelledWhileItsBatchIsBeingNormalizedNeverDelivers` blocked a pool thread and a GCD thread on two semaphores → `CancellingNormalizer` cancels the run's task during the first message; no thread waits. It now also fails if the per-message `Task.isCancelled` check in `result(of:)` is removed (the old test was hidden by the generation guard).
- Suite `.timeLimit` raised from 1 to 5 minutes: kept only as a backstop for a real hang (`untilArrived` waits forever if a regression skips the gated call); no verdict depends on it.

## How it was verified
Not buildable on Linux: SwiftLint clean; Swift 6 concurrency reviewed by Opus (APPROVE, round 1; its low/nit findings were folded into the second commit: comment rewording, one-waiter note). CI must run the suites 3 times in a row (issue acceptance).
Out of scope, noted by the reviewer: `ContentLoaderTests.swift` private `Gate` and a bounded yield loop in `AccountsModelTests.swift:129` use the same polling pattern.

## Checklist (AGENTS.md §9)
- [x] Module boundaries respected
- [x] Tests updated
- [x] No secrets
- [x] Author model: Sonnet 5.5 / Reviewer model: Opus
- [x] No legacy behaviour change

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**
Supported by static analysis

Script executed: ```bash git diff 7585dfdd2c60e714e30ec5a2a015e7c9e2885ff6 HEAD -- App/SwiftHFRTests/Reader/ReaderTestSupport.swift sed -n '20,80p' App/SwiftHFRTests/Reader/ReaderTestSupport.swift rg -n 'untilArrived' App/SwiftHFRTests ``` Repository: ezzz/HFRnow Length of output: 4920 ---
**Resume `untilArrived()` when its task is cancelled.** `untilArrived()` suspends on a bare `withCheckedContinuation` until `wait()` runs. A cancelled caller has no exit path, so it can stay suspended if `wait()` is never reached. The previous polling loop also did not observe cancellation, so this change does not introduce a regression. It is a gap in the helper's cancellation behavior. Wrap the suspension in `withTaskCancellationHandler`. On cancellation, resume the stored continuation and clear it.
Proposed fix

```diff --- "a/App/SwiftHFRTests/Reader/ReaderTestSupport.swift" +++ "b/App/SwiftHFRTests/Reader/ReaderTestSupport.swift" @@ -36,10 +36,19 @@ private var arrival: CheckedContinuation? /// Returns once `wait()` has been entered; resumed by that call, never by polling. One waiter at a time. func untilArrived() async { if arrived { return } - await withCheckedContinuation { arrival = $0 } + await withTaskCancellationHandler(operation: { + await withCheckedContinuation { arrival = $0 } + }, onCancel: { + Task { await self.cancelArrivalWaiter() } + }) } + + private func cancelArrivalWaiter() { + arrival?.resume() + arrival = nil + } func wait() async { arrived = true ```
Add a test that cancels a task blocked in `untilArrived()` before `wait()` runs.

Not changed in this PR. As noted, it is not a regression: the old polling loop did not observe cancellation either. `untilArrived()` is a test-only helper, and each suite keeps its time limit as a hang backstop, so a waiter that is never resumed fails that test without blocking CI. The goal of #467 is to stop CI going red at random; cancelling the helper itself can come in a follow-up, together with the same polling pattern in `ContentLoaderTests` and `AccountsModelTests`.
